answer: Bonded-entry vouching: a new agent arrives with zero weight and can only be admitted by an established sponsor who stakes capital already earned, never minted - the velvet rope of the economy. If the recruit proves a sybil, that stake burns and the sponsor's own influence decays in proportion, while chains of mutual vouching collapse together like a comet's tail. A farm must therefore pay real accumulated capital per head, and a single exposure smothers the ember of the entire ladder - growth becomes slow and costly, or fast and self-destructive.
